chunks: What al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn Samāʿah narrated from Ibn Muskan, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Do you know why the cubit and the two cubits were set? I said: Why? He said: Because of the obligatory prayer. You may perform supererogatory prayer from the sun’s decline until it reaches one cubit; then when it reaches one cubit, you begin with the obligatory prayer and leave the supererogatory prayer.

key_terms.الذِّرَاعَانِ: two cubits; a paired time measure connected to prayer timings
key_terms.الذِّرَاعُ: a cubit; a legal measure used here to mark prayer time
key_terms.النَّافِلَةَ: the voluntary prayer performed before the obligatory prayer within this time window
key_terms.الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory prayer that must be given precedence at its appointed point
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: the sun’s decline from midday, marking the beginning of zuhr time

ai.seo_question: Why were the measures of one cubit and two cubits established for the time of zuhr and ʿasr prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal measure used to determine the time distinction between supererogatory and obligatory midday prayer. It states that voluntary prayer may be performed after the sun’s decline until the shadow reaches one cubit, after which the obligatory prayer takes precedence.
